about.title: Point Arena Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Point Arena is small enough that a fender bender on Main Street tends to involve someone you recognize. That closeness can make the aftermath awkward, especially when the other driver's insurer starts calling. In the most recent final crash year on record, 2020, the city logged zero injury collisions, zero people injured and zero traffic deaths. Even so, the public record shows where collisions have clustered: Port Road, Route 1, Lake Street and Main Street carry the highest counts, and reported crashes have tended to peak on Monday evenings between 7 and 9 p.m. If you were hurt in one, the steps you take in the first few days matter. Photograph the vehicles, keep every medical record, and hold off on giving the other side's adjuster a recorded statement until you have talked with counsel. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Point Arena residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney who handles Mendocino County car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Point Arena Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people think
items.desc: California gives you two years to file a car accident injury claim, but if a government entity is involved, such as a claim tied to a state or county road, notice may be required within six months. An attorney can pin down which deadline applies to your crash before it passes.

items.title: Partial fault does not shut you out
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you share some blame for the collision. Your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated, and there is no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in an ordinary car accident case.

items.title: No upfront cost, and your evidence stays protected
items.desc: Every attorney in our network works on contingency, so you pay nothing unless there is a recovery. They also step in early to preserve photos, repair estimates and medical records, and to handle the insurer so you are not pressured into a recorded statement.

items.question: My crash was on Route 1 just outside Point Arena. Does that change my claim?
items.answer: It can. Route 1 is a state highway, so if a road condition or a public vehicle is alleged to have played a role, a claim against the responsible agency may need to be filed within six months rather than two years. Crashes on the highway are also often handled by a different responding agency than those in town, which affects where the report is kept. An attorney can sort out both issues quickly.

items.question: The other driver's insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it is generally wise to wait until you have spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use an offhand remark about how you feel or what you remember to reduce what they pay. You can be polite, confirm the basic facts of the collision, and decline to go on the record for now.

items.question: I think I was partly to blame. Is it still worth talking to an attorney?
items.answer: Yes. California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility but not wiped out, even if you were mostly at fault. In a small community like Point Arena, fault is sometimes assumed rather than proven, and an attorney can look at the evidence objectively. The consultation through LawProactive is free, so there is no cost to finding out where you stand.
